spans.s:
पण् 1. पण् (connected with rt. पन्, q. v.),
cl. 1. A. and 10. P. A. पणते, पणायति,
-ते, पेणे or पणायाञ्-चक्रे, अपणीत्, अपणिष्ट
or अपणायिष्ट, to honour, praise.

पण् 2. पण् (probably for original पर्ण्
fr. rt. पर् or पॄ), cl. 1. A. (ep. also P.)
पणते, -ति, पेणे, पणिष्यते, अपणिष्ट, पणि-
तुम्, to deal in, barter, purchase, buy; to negotiate,
bargain, transact business (Ved.); to bet or stake at
play (with gen. of the thing staked, e. g. शतस्य
पणते, he stakes a hundred); to play for (with
gen.); to stake anything or any person (acc.) on a
game; to risk or hazard (a battle &c.); to win
anything (inst.) from any one (acc.) at play; [cf.
बणिज्: Gr. πέπνημι: Lith. pantas: Old Germ.
feil; phant.]

पणस्य, Nom. P. पणस्यति, -यितुम्, to
honour; [cf. पनस्य.]
पणायित or पणित, अस्, आ, अम्, praised.
पणितव्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be praised.

पणितव्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be bought, vendible, fit
or intended for sale; to be transacted, negotiable.
पण्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be honoured or praised.

पण्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be sold, saleable, vendible;
to be transacted as business; (अम्), n. an article of
trade, a ware, commodity; trade, traffic, business; (आ), f.
heart-pea, Cardiospermum Halicacabum; [cf. पिण्या.]
—पण्य-ता, f. saleableness, the being an article of
trade.
—पण्यन्-ध or पण्यन्-धा, a species of
grass, Panicum Verticillatum.
—पण्य-पति, इस्, m.
a possessor of many wares, a great merchant, large
trader.
—पण्यपति-त्व, अम्, n. the state or con-
dition of a great merchant.
—पण्य-फल-त्व, अम्,
n. prosperity or profit in trade.
—पण्य-भूमि, इस्,
f. a place where goods are stored, a warehouse.
—पण्य-मूल्य, अम्, n. the price of a commodity.
—पण्य-योषित्, त्, f. a venal woman, prostitute,
wanton woman, courtezan, harlot, whore.
—पण्य-
विक्रय-शाला, f. a place for buying and selling, a
market-place, bazar.
—पण्य-विक्रयिन्, ई, m. a
seller of goods, a trader, merchant.
—पण्य-विला-
सिनी, f. a venal woman, a harlot; a kind of fragrant
substance, the claw of an animal or something
similar.
—पण्य-वीथिका, f. or पण्य-वीथी, f. a
place of sale, market; a stall, shop.
—पण्य-शाला,
f. a market, bazar, shop, a warehouse.
—पण्य-
स्त्री, f. or पण्याङ्गना (˚य-अङ्˚), f. a venal woman,
harlot, courtezan, prostitute.
—पण्याजिर (˚य-अज्˚),
अम्, n. a market.
—पण्याजीव (˚य-आज्˚), अस्, m. a
trader, tradesman; (अम्), n. a market, fair (?).
—पण्-
याजीवक (˚य-आज्˚), अम्, n. a market; (also, accord-
ing to some, पण्य-जीवक.)
—पण्यान्-धा, f. =
पण्यन्-धा, q. v.
—पण्यार्ह (˚य-अर्˚), अस्, आ,
अम्, fit for sale, saleable, vendible.

1. पाण्य, अस्, आ, अम्, (for 2. see p. 563), belonging
to the hand (Ved.); a patronymic (= कौण्डिन्य).

पाण्य 2. पाण्य, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. rt. 1. पण्),
praiseworthy, excellent. (
For. 1

. पाण्य see p. 562,
col. 3.)

पण, अस्, m. play, gaming, playing with dice,
playing for a stake; a game played for a stake, a
bet, a wager, (पणं कृ, to make a bet); the thing
staked or deposited; a sum played for; a compact,
contract, agreement; stipulation, treaty; wages, hire;
reward; expense of an expedition; a sum (reckoned
in coins or shells); a weight of copper (Manu

VII.
126

); a particular coin (= twenty Māṣas = four
Kākinīs); a particular measure; a handful of any-
thing; a commodity for sale; price; wealth, pro-
perty; business; a publican or distiller; a house,
dwelling (?).
—पण-काल, अस्, m. gaming-time,
time for playing.
—पण-ग्रन्थि, इस्, m. a fair,
[]
market.
—पण-ता, f. or पण-त्व, अम्, n. the state
or condition of a pledge or stake; price, value.
—पण-बन्ध, अस्, m. making a treaty, making
peace, pacification.
—पण-स्त्री, f. or पणाङ्गना
(˚ण-अङ्˚), f. a venal woman, a prostitute, harlot.
—पणार्पण (˚ण-अर्˚), अम्, n. making an
agreement, engagement, contract.
—पणार्ह (˚ण-
अर्˚), अस्, आ, अम्, fit to be laid as a wager.
—प-
णास्थि (˚ण-अस्˚), इ, n. Cypræa Moneta, the small
shell used as a die and as a coin, a cowrie.

पाण 1. पाण, अस्, m. (fr. rt. 2. पण्), a stake
at play, a game; trade, traffic; a trader; praise.
पाण 2. पाण. See col. 3.
2. पाण, अस्, m. = पाणि, the hand.

पणन, अम्, n. the act of bartering, purchasing;
traffic; sale, selling; betting.

पणनीय, अस्, आ, अम्, to be laid as a wager,
negotiable.

पणस, अस्, m. a commodity, an article of sale
or commerce (= पनस, q. v.).

पणाया, f. (probably an incorrect form), business,
affair, transaction, buying and selling, &c.; profits
and receipts of trade; a market-place.

पणि, इस्, m. (lit. ‘a negotiator or tradesman, one who
barters and traffics’), a miser, a niggard; one who is
sparing of sacrificial oblations; an impious man who
gives nothing to the gods, a Śūdra sacrificing priest;
N. of a class of envious demons watching over
treasures, (they are defeated by the gods and the
Aṅgirasas; sometimes the word पणि is only an
epithet of the Asuras who are supposed to steal
cows and hide them in mountain-caverns.)

पाणि पाणि, इस्, m. (perhaps akin to पर्ण;
said to be fr. rt. 2. पण्), the hand (in this sense
frequently at the end of a comp. describing that
which is carried in the hand, e. g. दर्भ-पाणि,
with Kuśa grass in the hand, carrying Kuśa grass;
cf. दण्ड-प्˚, शस्त्र-प्˚, समित्-प्˚); a hoof (Ved.);
a place of sale, shop, market; पाणिं ग्रह्, to take
the hand of a girl in the marriage ceremony, to
marry.
—पाणि-कच्छपिका, f. ‘hand-tortoise,’ a
particular position of the fingers.
—पाणि-कर्ण, अस्,
m. ‘hand-eared,’ ‘having hands for ears,’ one of the
epithets of Śiva.
—पाणिकूर्चन्, आ, m., N. of one
of the attendants of Skanda.
—पाणि-खात, अस्, आ,
अम्, ‘dug with the hand,’ N. of a sacred bathing-
place.
—पाणि-गृहीत, अस्, आ, अम्, taken by the
hand, seized; (ई), f. married according to the ritual,
a bride, wife.
—पाणि-ग्रह, अस्, m. or पाणि-ग्र-
हण, अम्, n. taking by the hand, taking the hand,
marrying, marriage (the joining of the bride and
bridegroom's hands forming part of the ceremony).
—पाणिग्रह-कर, अस्, m. one who performs (the
ceremony of) taking the hand; a lawful husband.
—पाणिग्रहणिक or पाणिग्रहणीय, अस्, ई, अम्,
relating to marriage, matrimonial, nuptial; (अम्), n.
a wedding present.
—पाणि-ग्रहीतृ, ता, m. ‘hand-
taker,’ one who has married, a bridegroom, husband.
—पाणि-ग्राह, अस्, m. taking the hand, marriage;
one who has married, a bridegroom, husband.
—पाणि-घ, अस्, m. ‘striking with the hand,’ a
drummer, one who plays on a tabor or other hand-
instrument; a workman, handicraftsman.
—पाणि-
घात, अस्, m. a blow with the hand; striking with
the hand, boxing; one who strikes with his hand, a
boxer.
—पाणि-घ्न, अस्, m., Ved. clapping the
hands.
—पाणि-चन्द्र, अस्, m., N. of a prince.
—पाणि-चापल्य, अम्, n. fidgeting with the hands,
snapping the fingers, &c.
—पाणि-ज, अस्, m. a finger-
nail.
—पाणि-तल, अम्, n. the palm or flat of the
hand; a particular weight (= 2 Tolakas); (ए), n. du.
the two palms.
—पाणि-धर्म, अस्, m. form of
marriage, manner of marrying.
—पाणिन्-धम,
अस्, आ, अम्, blowing through the hands; with
अध्वन्, a journey in which a person blows into his
hands, (perhaps) cold, chilly; obscure, dark (as a
path, where a noise is made with the hands to
frighten away snakes &c.).
—पाणिन्-धय, अस्, ई,
अम्, drinking out of the hands.
—पाणिन्-पल्लव, अस्,
अम्, m. n. ‘hand-twig,’ the fingers.
—पाणि-पात्र, अस्,
आ, अम्, ‘hand-cupped,’ using the hand as a drinking-
vessel, drinking out of the hand.
—पाणि-पाद, अम्,
n. the hands and feet.
—पाणि-पीडन, अम्, n. press-
ing the hand (of a bride), marriage.
—पाणि-पूर,
अस्, आ, अम्, filling the hand.
—पाणिप्रणयि-ता, f.
the state of being taken as a wife, wife-hood.
—पाणि-
प्रणयिन्, ई, इनी, इ, loved by the hand, being or
resting in the hand; (इनी), f. ‘beloved of the
hand,’ a wife.
—पाणि-प्रदान, अम्, n. giving
the hand (in confirmation of a promise).
—पाणि-
बन्ध, अस्, m. union or junction of the hands (in
marrying).
—पाणि-भुज्, क्, m. the glomerous fig-
[]
tree, Ficus Glomerata.
—पाणि-मत्, आन्, अती, अत्,
possessed of hands.
—पाणि-मर्द, अस्, m. Carissa
Carandas (= कर-मर्द).
—पाणि-मुक्त, अम्, n.,
scil. अस्त्र, a missile weapon, one thrown with the
hand, as a dart, spear.
—पाणि-मुख, अस्, ई, अम्, Ved.
‘hand-mouthed,’ having the hand for a mouth.
—पाणि-
मूल, अम्, n. the root of the hand, the extremity
of the arm.
—पाणि-रुह्, ट्, or पाणि-रुह, अस्, m. a
finger-nail.
—पाणि-वाद, अस्, m. ‘playing with the
hand,’ one who plays a drum or tabour, a drummer;
(अम्), n. clapping the hands together.
—पाणि-
वादक, अस्, m. ‘playing with the hand,’ one who
plays a drum or tabour, a drummer.
—पाणि-सङ्-
ग्रहण, अम्, n. clasping the hand (in confirmation
of a promise), shaking hands.
—पाणि-सर्ग्य, अस्,
आ, अम्, unwound and let out of the hand (as a rope).
—पाणि-सर्या (?), f. a rope or cord.
—पाणि-स्थ,
अस्, आ, अम्, being in the hand, held in the hand.
—पाणि-स्वनिक, अस्, m. one who plays musical
instruments with the hands.
—पाणि-हता, f., scil.
पुष्करिणी, N. of a lake (which the gods created
for Śākya-muni with a stroke of the hand).
—पाणौ-
करण, अम्, n. marriage.
—पाण्य्-आस्य, अस्, आ, अम्,
‘hand-mouthed,’ having the hand for a mouth; (अस्),
m. a Brāhman who reads the Vedas upon receiving
a gift at a Śrāddha.

पणिक, अस्, आ, अम्, at the end of an adj. comp.
(e. g. पञ्चाशत्-पणिक, [a fine] consisting of fifty
Paṇas).

पाणिक, अस्, m. a merchant; N. of one of the
attendants of Skanda; (आ), f. a kind of song or
singing; a sort of spoon or ladle.

पणित, अस्, आ, अम्, transacted as business; betted;
(अम्), n. a bet, wager, stake.

पणितृ, ता, त्री, तृ, one who transacts business
or traffics or sells; (ता), m. a trader, dealer.

पणफर पणफर, अम्, n. (fr. ἐπαναφορά),
the house following upon a Kendra, q. v. (in astrol.).

पणव पणव, अस्, m. (probably for प्र-
णव), a sort of musical instrument, a small drum
or tabor or a kind of cymbal, one used to accompany
singing; also (आ), f. a kind of metre consisting of
four lines of ten or five syllables each.

पणविन्, ई, इनी, इ, possessing a drum; (ई), m. an
epithet of Śiva.

पण्ड् पण्ड्, cl. 1. A. पण्डते, to go,
move; cl. 10. P. पण्डयति, &c., to
[]
collect, heap together, pile up; cl. 1. P. पण्डति;
cl. 10. P. पण्डयति, to destroy, annihilate.

पण्ड, अस्, or पण्डु, उस्, m. (said to be fr. rt. 2.
पण्), a eunuch, impotent man [cf. पण्ड्र, षण्ड];
(आ), f. wisdom, intelligence, understanding; science,
learning.
—पण्डापूर्व (˚ड-अप्˚), अम्, n. non-
occurrence of the results of fate or destiny (?).

पण्डक or पण्डग, अस्, m. (probably fr. पण्-
ड्रक), a eunuch; N. of one of the sons of the
third Manu Sāvarṇa.
पाण्डक पाण्डक, अस्, m., N. of a teacher.

पण्डित, अस्, आ, अम् [cf. पण्डा], learned, wise;
shrewd, skilled, clever, educated; (अस्), m. a scholar,
learned or wise man, learned Brāhman, teacher, phi-
losopher, Pandit; an adept, proficient; N. of a man;
incense.
—पण्डित-जातीय, अस्, आ, अम्, somewhat
clever, rather learned.
—पण्डित-ता, f. or पण्डित-
त्व, अम्, n. learning, knowledge, wisdom, skilful-
ness, cleverness.
—पण्डित-बुद्धि, इस्, इस्, इ, philo-
sophically minded.
—पण्डित-मण्डल, अम्, n.
an assembly or circle of learned men.
—पण्डित-
मानिक, अस्, आ, अम्, or पण्डित-मानिन्, ई, इनी, इ,
or पण्डितम्-मन्य, अस्, आ, अम्, fancying one's self
learned or clever; an ignorant and conceited person,
a pedant who thinks himself a Pandit.
—पण्डि-
तम्-मन्यमान, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. fancying one's
self learned.
—पण्डित-राज, अस्, m. ‘the prince of
the learned,’ an epithet of a great scholar.
—पण्डित-
वादिन्, ई, इनी, इ, pretending to be wise.
—पण्डित-
सभा, f. an assembly of Pandits or literati.

पण्डितक, अस्, आ, अम्, wise, learned; (अस्), m. a
learned man; N. of one of the sons of Dhṛta-rāṣṭra.

पण्डिताय, Nom. A. पण्डितायते, &c., to be-
come learned or wise.

पण्डितायमान, अस्, आ, अम्, becoming wise or
learned.
पण्डितिमन्, आ, m. wisdom, learning, scholarship.
पण्ड्र पण्ड्र or पण्ड्रक, अस्, m. a eunuch.

पाणिन्, ई, इनी, इ, at the end of an adj. comp. for
पाणि [cf. शस्त्र-प्˚, शूल-प्˚]; (इनस्), m. pl., N. of
a family reckoned among the Kauśikas.

पाणीतल, अम्, n. a particular measure (= 2 To-
lakas).

पाणिन पाणिन, अस्, m. said to = पाणिनि,
and according to some a patronymic from Paṇin.

पाणिनि, इस्, m. (probably fr. पाणिन above), N.
of the most eminent Hindū grammarian (regarded
as an inspired Muni; according to one legend his
grandfather was an inspired legislator called Devala,
and his mother's name was Dākṣī, see दाक्षेय;
the date at which he lived is a subject of controversy,
but he is generally placed in the middle of the
fourth century B. C.; from Śalātura, thought to
have been the dwelling-place of his ancestors, he is
said by some to have been called Śālāturīya; cf.
Pāṇ.

पाणिनीय, अस्, आ, अम्, relating to Pāṇini, written
or composed by Pāṇini; (अस्), m. a disciple or fol-
lower of Pāṇini, one who follows the system of
Pāṇini; an adherent or admirer of Pāṇini; (अम्),
n. (with or without व्य्-आकरण) the grammar of
Pāṇini.
—पाणिनीय-दर्शन, अम्, n., N. of a
chapter of the Sarva-darśana-saṅgraha.
—पाणिनीय-
मत-दर्पण, अम्, n. ‘mirror of the system of
Pāṇini,’ N. of a work.

पाणीतक पाणीतक, अस्, m., N. of a being
attendant upon Skanda; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a people,
(a various reading for करीति.)

पाण्डर पाण्डर, पाण्डव. See p. 563,
col. 1.

पाण्डर, अस्, आ, अम्, whitish-yellow, whitish,
white; (अस्), m. a species of plant (= मरु-वक);
N. of a mountain; of a Nāga; of a sect; (अम्), n.
the blossom of the jasmine; red chalk, ruddle.
—पाण्डर-द्वार-गो-पुर, अस्, आ, अम्, having
white doors and city gates.
—पाण्डर-पुष्पिका, f.
a species of plant (= शीतला).
—पाण्डर-भिक्षु,
उस्, m. ‘a white-robed mendicant,’ epithet of a par-
ticular sect.

पाण्डित्य पाण्डित्य, अम्, n. (fr. पण्डित),
scholarship, erudition, learning; cleverness, skill,
dexterity.

पाण्डु पाण्डु, उस्, उस्, उ (said to be fr. rt.
पण्ड्), yellowish white, white, pale; (उस्), m. pale
or yellowish white colour; jaundice; N. of two
plants, Trichosanthes Diœca (= पाण्डुर-फली);
a white elephant; N. of a prince, a son of Vyāsa by
the wife of Vicitra-vīrya and brother of Dhṛta-
rāṣṭra and Vidura; of a son of Janam-ejaya and
brother of Dhṛta-rāṣṭra; of a son of Dhātṛ by
Āyatī (according to others he is called Prāṇa); of an
attendant of Śiva; of a Nāga-rāja; of a people in
[]
Madhya-deśa; (उस्), f. a species of plant, Glycine
Debilis (commonly called Maṣāṇi); [cf. Hib.
buidhe, ‘yellow.’]
—पाण्डु-कण्टक, अस्, m. Achy-
ranthes Aspera (= अपा-मार्ग).
—पाण्डु-कम्बल,
अस्, m. a white woollen covering or blanket; a warm
upper garment; the housings of a royal elephant; a
kind of stone (limestone or marble ?).
—पाण्डु-
कम्बलिन्, ई, इनी, इ, covered with a white woollen
blanket; (ई), m. a carriage covered with a sort of
blanket; the housings of a royal elephant.
—पाण्-
डु-करण, अम्, or पाण्डु-कर्मन्, अ, n. (in
medicine) making or rendering white.
—पाण्डु-
तरु, उस्, m. Grislea Tomentosa (= धव).
—पाण्-
डु-ता, f. or पाण्डु-त्व, अम्, n. whitish-yellow
colour, paleness.
—पाण्डु-तीर्थ, अम्, n., N. of a
Tīrtha.
—पाण्डु-दुकूल, अम्, n. a white winding-
sheet.
—पाण्डुदुकूल-सीवन, अम्, n. ‘sewing of
the white winding-sheet,’ N. of a place where
Śākya-muni made a white winding-sheet.
—पाण्डु-
नाग, अस्, m. a white elephant; the plant Rottleria
Tinctoria.
—पाण्डु-पत्त्र-ता, f., Ved. the growing
yellow of leaves.
—पाण्डु-पत्त्री, f. = रेणुका, a
species of fragrant substance.
—पाण्डु-पुत्र, अस्,
m. a son of Pāṇḍu, any one of the Pāṇḍava princes;
(there are many similar compounds, as पाण्डु-
नन्दन, &c.)
—पाण्डु-पृष्ठ, अस्, आ, अम्,
white-backed, having no distinguished or auspicious
mark on the body, one from whom nothing great
is to be expected.
—पाण्डु-फल, अस्, m. ‘having
yellow fruit,’ Trichosanthes Diœca; (आ), f. a species
of gourd (= चिर्भिटा); (ई), f. = पाण्डुर-फली.
—पाण्डु-भाव, अस्, m. becoming yellowish-white.
—पाण्डु-भूम, अस्, आ, अम्, having a white, chalky
soil; (अस्), m. a country with a light-coloured soil.
—पाण्डु-मृत्तिक, अस्, आ, अम्, having a white,
chalky soil, consisting of chalk; (आ), f. a pale soil;
the opal.
—पाण्डु-मृद्, त्, f. chalk, a chalky soil,
a country in which the soil is of a whitish colour.
—पाण्डु-रङ्ग, अस्, m. a kind of vegetable (com-
monly called पाटराङ्गा).
—पाण्डु-राग, अस्, m.
Artemisia Indica; whiteness, pallor.
—पाण्डु-रोग,
अस्, m. ‘yellow disease,’ jaundice.
—पाण्डुरोगिन्, ई,
इणी, इ, suffering from jaundice, jaundiced.
—पाण्डु-
लेख, अम्, n. an outline or sketch made with a style
or with chalk.
—पाण्डु-लोमशा or पाण्डु-लोमा, f.
Glycine Debilis.
—पाण्डु-वर्ण, अस्, आ, अम्, pale-
coloured, white; (अस्), m. whiteness.
—पाण्डु-वर्म-
देव, अस्, m., N. of a prince.
—पाण्डु-शर्करा,
f. light-coloured gravel (the disease).
—पाण्डु-शर्-
मिला, f. an epithet of Draupadī the wife of the
sons of Pāṇḍu.
—पाण्डु-सोपाक, अस्, m. a particular
mixed caste, the offspring of a Caṇḍāla by a Vaidehī
mother (whose occupation, according to Manu

, is working with bamboos and reeds, making
baskets, mats, &c.).
—पाण्ड्व्-आमय, अस्, m. ‘yellow
disease,’ jaundice.
—पाण्ड्वामयिन्, ई, इनी, इ, suffer-
ing from jaundice, jaundiced.
पाण्डरक, अस्, m., N. of a Nāga-rāja.

पाण्डव, अस्, m. a patronymic, a son or descendant
of Pāṇḍu; a partisan of the sons of Pāṇḍu; N. of a
mountain; (आस्), m. pl. the five reputed sons of
Pāṇḍu (Yudhi-ṣṭhira, Bhīma, Arjuna, Nakula, and
Saha-deva; cf. कुन्ती and माद्री); the party or
adherents of the sons of Pāṇḍu; (अस्, ई, अम्), be-
longing to the sons of Pāṇḍu, connected with the
five Pāṇḍavas.
—पाण्डव-नकुल, अस्, m., N. of a
poet.
—पाण्डव-वह्नि, अयस्, m. pl. ‘the Pāṇḍava
fires,’ a N. applied to the three elder sons of Pāṇḍu
(‘kindled on the Araṇi, Pṛthā or Kuntī;’ cf. पृथा-
रणि).
—पाण्डव-श्रेष्ठ, अस्, m. ‘best of the
sons of Pāṇḍu,’ an epithet of Yudhi-ṣṭhria.
—पाण्-
डवाभील (˚व-आभ्˚), अस्, m. an epithet of Kṛṣṇa.

पाण्डवीय, अस्, आ, अम्, relating to the children of
Pāṇḍu, happening to the Pāṇḍavas.
पाण्डवेय = पाण्डव, q. v.

पाण्डुक, अस्, आ, अम्, = पाण्डु; (अस्), m. a pale or
yellowish-white colour; the jaundice; N. of a prince
(= पाण्डु); a species of rice; N. of one of the
nine treasures of the Jainas; (अम्), n., N. of a par-
ticular forest.

पाण्डूक, अस्, m., Ved. a species of rice; [cf.
पाण्डुक.]

पाण्डुकिन्, ई, इनी, इ, suffering from jaundice,
jaundiced.

पाण्डुर, अस्, आ, अम्, whitish, white, pale, yel-
lowish-white; (अस्), m. a form of jaundice; a species
of plant (= मरु-वक); N. of a being attendant
upon Skanda; (आ), f. Glycine Debilis (= माष-
पर्णी); (अम्), n. the white leprosy, vitiligo.
—पाण्-
डुर-ता, f. whiteness, white colour.
—पाण्डुर-
द्रुम, अस्, m. ‘the pale tree,’ Wrightia Antidy-
senterica.
—पाण्डुर-पृष्ठ, अस्, आ, अम्, = पाण्डु-
पृष्ठ, q. v.
—पाण्डुर-फली, f. a species of shrub
(= पाण्डु-फली, पाण्डु, धूसरा, &c.).
—पाण्-
डुरेक्षु (˚र-इक्˚), उस्, m. ‘pale sugar-cane,’ a
species of sugar-cane (= श्वेतेक्षु).
पाण्डुरिमन्, आ, m. pale or white colour, paleness.

पाण्ड्य, आस्, m. pl., N. of a people and of the
country in the Dekhan inhabited by them; (अस्), m.
a prince of the Pāṇḍyas; N. of a son of Ā-krīḍa;
N. of the mountain-range in the Pāṇḍya country.
—पाण्ड्य-देश, अस्, m. the country of the Pāṇḍyas.
—पाण्ड्य-वाट, Ved., N. of a district in which
pearls are found.
पणयितृ, ता, त्री, तृ, one who buys, a purchaser.
